notes.title: Community Items are available
notes.content:
Hey everyone,
Some of you may have noticed that I released the Steam community items! You can now earn trading cards, badges, backgrounds, emoticon and animated stickers from the world of Exophobia!

I think they turned out pretty cool. I'm not familiar with the Steam meta for items, but hope you have a good time with them. I got some cards retroactively, so I think it happened to all of you too!

On a sad note, I took some time to post this announcement after hitting the release button on the anniversary, because I've been feeling a bit down lately due to recent news.

A friend of mine, Filipe Duarte Pina has passed away due to cancer, at the very young age of 46. This came to me as a shock as he kept his condition secret. 
He was a legend in the portuguese game dev and comic book scene. He started out as a personal hero when I was just starting in game dev, as he was a pioneer having launched the first portuguese Playstation game as one of his highest achievements, and much more. I eventually got the opportunity to work for him at Nerd Monkeys, on the sequel for his dear Case and Bot point and click game that he produced. We became more than co-workers, but friends, as his charming personality and permanent good mood made everyone feel connected to him one way or another. My last interaction with him was a christmas dinner where I gave him a phyiscal copy of Exophobia. In a way, he was my game development mentor, and I hope he was proud of what I achieved after learning so much from him. He will be missed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/1fd15e14768800d5505a93d314365b3cd03c7b24.png[/img]
[i]A pixel depiction of Filipe and me made by him for the Express Killer[/i]


[hr][/hr]

His legacy will live on, on his work and the people dear to him. 
If you're curious about some of his work, here is a post-mortem of the Case and Bot games in english:
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sq4t7bG9Gsk]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sq4t7bG9Gsk[/url]

Best,

notes.title: Exophobia 1st Anniversary!
notes.content:
[p]Hey everyone! Long time no see...[/p][p]I've been super busy with work (yeah, got a full time job doing something else ːsteammockingː), so there hasn't been much Exophobia updating.[/p][p]I wish at this time I would have added way more stuff to the game. Nevertheless, I took this special date to update the game with the promised Lovecraftian update and run a 30% discount for the week![/p][p]Also, health pills are now cake for today lol

This update contains spoilers, so I will be discussing it below:[/p][p] [spoiler]The Lovecraftian update consists on the addition of a second phase to one boss.[/spoiler][/p][p][spoiler]This last boss fight is unlocked by getting the "true" ending (returning all gems to the emergency hatch)[/spoiler] [spoiler]You fight the Alien King a top the emergency pod returning to Earth.[/spoiler] [/p][p][spoiler]I always felt this fight didn't make justice to a climatic finale.[/spoiler] [/p][p][spoiler]Right now this fight gets a much needed second phase and balancing on the first phase to make it fair for people who haven't got the boss rush achievement yet! Thanks for making this year very special. I have some ideas on more content to add to the game, but still not sure everything will be possible. I want to do this as a thank you to all the players as I don't have the exact means to deliver them, but I will try!

notes.title: Exophobia nominated for Best Iberoamerican Videogame Animation!
notes.content:
Hey! First time posting since the new year! Hope you are all doing well and happy with how the year is going so far. For me it has been progressing at light speed, and excited with the potential of great things coming up this year.

I'm just taking the time to announce that Exophobia got nominated at Quirino Awards, for the category of Best Iberoamerican Videogame Animation! 
I'm going to be honest, I wasn't expecting my pixel art to have a chance at competing with the other games in the same category. I submitted it just because, well, there usually isn't much portuguese representation in stuff like this, and it is an IBERIAN award show after all.
But as a big fan of the animation medium, as in cartoons, shorts and yes, videogames, this gives me a lot of motivation to push my art to new places :) even if I never felt like a full artist myself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/24c5c121007378bfaa14227a0460dbb6dc305ec7.jpg[/img]

So here's some positive news about the game, with a tease of something more to come this year. I haven't been focusing too much on it yet (I'm taking my time with sorting all other aspects of my life first) but I'm slowly getting more and more excited to eventually update this game with new content!

So see you soon, and keep working on those new years resolutions!
Best,

notes.title: Exophobia Demo Update!
notes.content:
Hey there!
As promised and part of FPS Fest, the demo has been sligthly improved to better reflect the quality of the final game. Testing has been crucial to find these small quirks and how to adjust them. You may not notice any differences, so let me present you the changes in this new version:

[list]
[*] Some language errors fixed.
[*] Disk image in the corner to indicate a loading time.
[*] [i]"Sci-fi"[/i] font option is now a more readable font in the terminal.
[*] Map no longer starts to fade right away. Only when it reaches the last point in the battery.
[*] Clickable buttons and levers now blink to indicate you can use an action on them.
[*] You can now dash forward even if not holding a direction. Also, more i-frames!
[*] Difficulty curve in the first part of the game has been adjusted. Less enemies before you get the first upgrade (for me where the fun of the game comes).
[*] The boss now stays locked in the same vulnerable move until you hit. I made it that way so you can more easily guess what you have to do and so you don't have to wait until he cycles through all moves again to hit him.
[/list]

Can't even tell how long I have been revising this first part of the game, but I know it's the most important part to get right, so I hope these changes please all of you and incentivize you to keep playing!
Let me know what you think. 
More news coming soon!

notes.title: Exophobia at Metroidvania Fusion!
notes.content:
From March 4th to 11th, Exophobia is joining more than 170 other games in a Steam event all about metroidvanias, hosted by Ravenage Games.

Here you will find discounts in the most iconic games of the genre, or play demos of upcoming gems!

[b]Why is Exophobia considered a metroidvania?[/b]
Most metroidvania fans will argue that a metroidvania (metroid + castlevania for those who don't know) needs to be a sidescroller. 
My idea with Exophobia was to mix metroidvania progression with a first person shooter and I think it fits pretty well! Let's see, for example, where a Metroid game and Wolfenstein 3d can meet in the middle:

[list]
[*] Labyrinthic non-linear levels with gates that can only be opened with upgrades? [i]check[/i]
[*] Secrets around every corner or hidden wall that reward the player with powerups or easter eggs? [i]check[/i]
[*] Different biomes with different enemies and boss fights? [i]check[/i]
[/list]
Exophobia features all of this and more elements from both genres, like metroidvania checkpoints and fast paced shooter combat from first person shooters.

Let me know what you think! Meanwhile, play the demo and enjoy all the other available games in the event :)
Happy exploration!

notes.title: Going Rogue: A Festival of Persistence - Can a FPS also be a Metroidvania?
notes.content:
Hey everyone!
Exophobia has been selected to be part of a Steam festival all about roguelikes, rogue-lites, souls-likes and [b]metroidvanias[/b], called [url=https://store.steampowered.com/category/going_rogue/]Going Rogue: A Festival of Persistence [/url]!

I was a bit surprised to see Steam inviting me to be part of a festival with this name, until I saw metroidvanias were part of the list of celebrated types of games. And metroidvania is one of Exophobia's most prominent tag, and this is where the game's inclusion might start to sound controversial. But here is how I designed Exophobia to feel like a METROIDVANIA FPS! 

Steam defines games eligible for this festival with "[i]These games generally share mechanics of repeating parts of the game again and again, or re-treading ground once the player has gained enough experience or equipment."[/i]

Even though metroidvanias are often thought as 2D platformers, progression in Exophobia was designed to feature these ideas as an FPS with no verticality (quite a challenge!).
The gameplay happens inside the spaceship, a giant map with multiple floors each having their own characteristics (look, enemies, objects,...), with multiple gated areas, designed to push exploration. The player progresses through the game by finding upgrades, that improve combat mechanics as well as uncover areas that were locked before. The more you progress, the more the map opens up, and you might even find secrets that you can now access with your new abilities as you backtrack to find your next one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/9d0e89bbc337ccd303dccd8b03fc79a1d2e625d0.png[/img]

Besides this larger progression loop, you can also find other gated areas with one-way doors, key cards, movement challenging areas and even boss fights can unlock something on the map! You also have to save often in checkpoints, because that's where you return when you die, something you also see in metroidvanias.

So, in brief:
[list]
[*]One giant map with different themed areas and checkpoints.[i]Check[/i]
[*]A clear player power arc and enjoyable movement. [i]Check[/i]
[*]Gates, boss fights and hidden secrets to reward exploration. [i]Check[/i]
[/list]

Of course, feel free to give your own opinions on the subject :)
Have some great runs with the festival,
Zarc [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/a6e1c15b56e6222c21b0db0b2528a7ea29c35e23.png[/img]

notes.content:

[/h3]

You can always join the [url=https://discord.gg/Qb5Kd3p]Zarc Attack Discord[/url] to chat with me and other fans. 

Also, due to some requests,[h3][b] I will keep the demo available for the next couple of days.[/b]

Here's some extra challenges if you want to replay the demo:
[list]
[*]  Collect all discs (5/5)
[*]  Collect all health upgrades (3/3)
[*]  Push an enemy into the conveyor belt end
[*]  Lure an alien into some lasers
[*]  Find the hidden helmet powerup (3/3)
[*]  Beat the final boss with no damage
[/list]

notes.title: Steam Game Festival - Exophobia Quick Pitch
notes.content:
Hello there, I'm José Castanheira, aka 'Zarc' [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/a6e1c15b56e6222c21b0db0b2528a7ea29c35e23.png[/img]

I'm a solo dev developing Exophobia, a modern, clean take on the classic retro first-person shooter gameplay, combining a frightening sci-fi setting, a stylized aesthetic, fast-paced intense combat and metroidvania exploration.

Imagine if Wolfenstein 3D was never upgraded upon, but evolved with faster and more intense gameplay. Mix that with alien enemies, tough bosses, upgradeable character and a rhythmic synthwave OST! (by [url=https://joaopcosta.bandcamp.com/]Pedro J. Costa[/url])

In this demo, you'll be able to play a short level featuring the first elements of the game, from getting equipped with the weapon to fighting the first boss. I promise that it's filled with a lot of great moments, hope you enjoy it!

Have fun, Zarc [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36143584/a6e1c15b56e6222c21b0db0b2528a7ea29c35e23.png[/img]
